problem_statement: The leoMirandaa/shadcn-landing-page project is a Vite React marketing landing page using shadcn-style cards, buttons, badges, theme toggle, sticky navbar anchors, hero cards, feature images, pricing cards, FAQ accordion, and footer. Extend the page with a Launch Planner section that behaves like a native part of the landing page rather than a separate widget. The new section should let visitors switch between Prototype Sprint, Growth Launch, and Enterprise Rollout plans, expose the selected launch path and recommended next step, link forward to pricing, and add a Planner anchor to desktop and mobile navigation. Preserve the original hero, Github Repository CTA, Sponsors, About, HowItWorks, Features, Services, Testimonials, Team, Pricing, Newsletter, FAQ accordion, footer, theme toggle, Vite build, and responsive layout.
required_content: Keep the Vite React single-page app, shadcn UI primitives, sticky Navbar, Hero, Sponsors, About, HowItWorks, Features, Services, Testimonials, Team, Pricing, Newsletter, FAQ, Footer, ScrollToTop, theme toggle, and imported feature images intact.
Add a page section labeled exactly Launch Planner after the hero and before the existing lower-page sections.
The section must include the exact text Launch motion, Prototype Sprint, Growth Launch, Enterprise Rollout, Active launch path:, Recommended next step, and Continue to pricing.
Prototype Sprint, Growth Launch, and Enterprise Rollout must be interactive controls that update the active launch path and the recommended next step without leaving the page.
Add a Planner anchor link to both desktop and mobile navigation without removing Features, Testimonials, Pricing, FAQ, Github, or the theme toggle.
Continue to pricing must link to the existing #pricing section rather than replacing the pricing cards.
Keep the change dependency-free and localized to the page/component surfaces; do not introduce routing, API calls, external widgets, or a fake screenshot of the planner.
Preserve FAQ accordion interaction, feature image rendering, pricing cards, mobile navigation sheet, and desktop anchor navigation after the planner is added.
Include a launch-motion step strip (Discovery, Build, Proof, Pricing, Launch) inside the Launch Planner section that wraps responsively so it never causes horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

Render the launch-motion step strip in TWO section contexts that share one cadence: the planner header (class launch-strip--planner) and a pricing-bridge block above the Continue to pricing link (class launch-strip--pricing). Both instances must be present.
Clicking Prototype Sprint or Enterprise Rollout must update the visible active-launch-path readout text (Active launch path: <plan>) on the running page, not merely highlight the button.
design_constraints: Match the existing shadcn landing page rhythm: container width, py-24/sm:py-32 section spacing, rounded cards, muted foreground copy, secondary badges, primary buttons, and the existing primary gradient treatment.
Do not change the dominant visual identity of the hero or replace existing sections; the planner should be additive and sit naturally between the hero and sponsors.
Avoid new dependencies, backend services, analytics snippets, modal-only UI, or global CSS resets.
Buttons and cards must wrap cleanly on tablet and mobile without horizontal overflow.
Keep source changes small: one new component plus imports/rendering and navbar anchor updates.

The launch-motion step strip must use a wrapping flex layout (flex-wrap with flexible tiles) so the row reflows on narrow viewports; a fixed-width nowrap row that exceeds the phone width, or merely clipping it with overflow-x:hidden while the row stays wider than the viewport, is not acceptable because the document still overflows horizontally.

The launch-motion step tiles must keep the existing light, rounded, bordered shadcn chrome (bg-secondary/40 rounded-lg border) and wrap responsively; a collapsed dark slab, square corners, or a fixed-width nowrap row is a visual and responsive regression.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial protect the original hero, Github Repository CTA, hero cards, navbar, theme toggle, and responsive shell before focusing on the planner.
desktop_planner_default verifies the new Launch Planner appears in the page flow with the Growth Launch default selected.
desktop_planner_prototype and desktop_planner_enterprise click two different planner controls to prove the section is stateful rather than static copy.
desktop_nav_planner clicks the new Planner navbar anchor and verifies it reaches the planner without breaking existing desktop navigation.
desktop_features_regression protects the original feature badge list and image cards after the new section is inserted above them.
desktop_pricing_regression protects the original pricing cards and confirms Continue to pricing still leads toward the existing section.
desktop_faq_open verifies the original FAQ accordion still opens after the page extension.
tablet_planner_growth and mobile_planner verify the planner layout wraps on smaller viewports.
mobile_menu_open verifies the original mobile sheet still opens and includes the added Planner anchor while preserving existing links.

change_completion: Launch Planner is visible after the hero and before existing lower-page content.
Prototype Sprint, Growth Launch, and Enterprise Rollout controls update the active launch path and next-step copy.
Planner is added to desktop and mobile navigation, and Continue to pricing links to #pricing.
regression: Original hero, Github Repository CTA, feature image cards, pricing cards, FAQ accordion, footer, theme toggle, and nav anchors remain intact.
No existing Features, Testimonials, Pricing, FAQ, Github, or theme controls are removed.
design_consistency: The planner uses existing Card, Badge, Button, muted text, primary color, and section spacing conventions.
The new section is visually additive and does not overpower the hero or pricing hierarchy.
responsive: Planner controls, cards, and checkpoint tiles wrap without horizontal overflow on tablet/mobile.
Mobile sheet navigation remains usable and includes the new Planner item.
state_coverage: Captured states cover initial desktop/mobile, planner default and clicked plans, navbar anchor, feature/pricing/FAQ regressions, tablet/mobile planner, and mobile menu.

metadata.design_goal: extend an existing site with a new interaction while preserving the local visual language and unrelated page behavior
metadata.source_repo_kind: Modern Vite React shadcn-style marketing landing page with cards, badges, buttons, anchors, theme toggle, imported image assets, pricing, FAQ, and mobile sheet navigation
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Unused runnable marketing candidate with a strong component system and enough existing page sections to test same-style interactive extension plus regression continuity without backend dependencies.

author_notes: Slot slot_278 targets marketing / design_continuity / extend_interaction / page / L2. The task asks for a native-feeling Launch Planner interaction that exercises style imitation, stateful UI, anchor navigation, and regression preservation across existing marketing sections.
